title: Center hope where the wandering mind cannot rule
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 273
summary: This shabad opens by showing the God-conscious being resting hope in the One alone. It turns the heart toward gathered hope, disciplined mind, and shared remembrance.
whyItMatters: This one speaks to the person whose attachment, distraction, or doubt keeps scattering the heart. It teaches a steadier center than private grasping can provide.
takeaway: Hope steadies when it is centered in the One.

lines.translation: The God-conscious being centers his hopes on the One alone.
The God-conscious being shall never perish.
The God-conscious being is steeped in humility.
The God-conscious being delights in doing good to others.
The God-conscious being has no worldly entanglements.
The God-conscious being holds his wandering mind under control.

lines.gurmukhi: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਕੈ ਹੋਇ ਸੁ ਭਲਾ ॥
lines.transliteration: braham giaanee kai hoi su bhalaa ||
lines.translation: The God-conscious being acts in the common good.
The God-conscious being blossoms in fruitfulness.
In the Company of the God-conscious being, all are saved.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਜਪੈ ਸਗਲ ਸੰਸਾਰੁ ॥੪॥
lines.transliteration: naanak braham giaanee japai sagal sa(n)saar ||4||
lines.translation: O Nanak, through the God-conscious being, the whole world meditates on God. ||4||

structure: The shabad begins by gathering hope into a single center.
From there it shows the wandering mind being brought under truthful rule.
The closing movement rests by widening that steadiness into remembrance that benefits more than the self.
